raw_prompt:
Respond in English.

Problem: <<<USER_INPUT>>>
Open-source AI models democratize access to powerful technology, but they also enable malicious actors to bypass safety guardrails. Some argue that the benefits of open-weight models (transparency, innovation, decentralization) outweigh the risks, while others contend that the potential for harm (disinformation, cyberattacks, bioweapon design) makes unrestricted release irresponsible. Resolve this tension.
<<<END_USER_INPUT>>>

Thesis: Unrestricted open-weight AI models are ethically mandatory and strategically superior because centralized control concentrates dangerous power while transparency enables the global community to audit and mitigate risks more effectively than proprietary black boxes.
Antithesis: Restricted open-weight AI models and centralized safety oversight are ethically mandatory and strategically superior because unrestricted distribution accelerates existential risk faster than transparency can mitigate it, and effective safety requires controlled deployment rather than open access.
Compatible contradictions: [
  "The thesis claims transparency enables mitigation, yet unrestricted release renders post-deployment auditing ineffective against immediate malicious exploitation.",
  "The thesis rejects centralized power as dangerous, yet enforcing safety boundaries and preventing misuse fundamentally requires centralized authority and control."
]
Synthesis candidates: [
  "Transparency enables broader community auditing and prevents dangerous concentration of AI power.",
  "Risk mitigation requires controlled deployment and boundaries to prevent immediate catastrophic misuse."
]

Perform Aufhebung: a qualitatively higher position that transcends both. This is NOT a compromise — it must contain genuine novelty.

Output JSON: {"aufhebung": "<higher position>", "preserved_from_thesis": ["<truth kept>"], "preserved_from_antithesis": ["<truth kept>"], "transcended": "<what was left behind>", "new_insights": ["<genuine novelty>"]}
